required_sets.match: Journal|Law Review|L\. ?Rev|L\. ?J\.|Hansard|Debates|Osgoode|McGill|Queen's|Dalhousie|Alberta Law|Manitoba Law|UBC Law|Ottawa Law
required_sets.note: one journal article or Hansard debate with its actual pinpoint

required_quotations.quote: the duty arises when the Crown has knowledge, real or constructive, of the potential existence of the Aboriginal right or title and contemplates conduct that might adversely affect it

definitions.ISSUE-01: When the duty to consult is triggered and whether a regulator's approval decision is Crown conduct that triggers it.
definitions.ISSUE-02: Where on the Haida spectrum the consultation falls and what meaningful consultation and accommodation require, contrasting Tsleil-Waututh and Coldwater.
definitions.ISSUE-03: Whether the Nation can insist on consent or a veto, and whether the duty attaches to Parliament's law-making.
definitions.ISSUE-04: What the UNDRIP Act and the Impact Assessment Act add, by section.
definitions.ISSUE-05: One journal article or Hansard debate bearing on the question, with its actual pinpoint.
definitions.PROP-01: The duty arises when the Crown has knowledge, real or constructive, of the potential existence of the Aboriginal right or title and contemplates conduct that might adversely affect it (Haida para 35).
definitions.PROP-02: Consultation runs along a spectrum from notice to deep consultation depending on the strength of the claim and the seriousness of the potential effect (Haida paras 43 to 45).
definitions.PROP-03: The trigger has three elements: Crown knowledge, contemplated Crown conduct, and the potential that the conduct adversely affects the claim or right (Rio Tinto para 31).
definitions.PROP-04: Past wrongs or continuing effects of earlier decisions do not alone trigger a fresh duty; the contemplated conduct must put current claims and rights in jeopardy (Rio Tinto paras 48, 49 and 54).
definitions.PROP-05: The Crown may rely on a regulatory agency's process to fulfil the duty, ultimate responsibility remaining with the Crown; in Clyde River the consultation fell short and the duty was breached (Clyde River paras 30, 45 and 53).
definitions.PROP-07: The NEB process was sufficient to satisfy the duty in Chippewas of the Thames; the Crown may rely on an agency with the statutory powers to do what the duty requires (Chippewas paras 32, 51 and 66).
definitions.PROP-08: The law-making process does not constitute Crown conduct that triggers the duty to consult (Mikisew 2018 para 2, Karakatsanis J.; para 102, Brown J. concurring).
definitions.PROP-09: Section 35 gives no veto over development; where adequate consultation has occurred a development may proceed without consent, and the process is one of give and take (Ktunaxa paras 83 and 114).
definitions.PROP-10: The consultation decision is reviewed for reasonableness (Ktunaxa para 77).
definitions.PROP-11: Reasonableness, not perfection, is the standard; the renewed Trans Mountain consultation was reasonable (Coldwater paras 27, 77 and 83).
definitions.PROP-12: Phase III of the earlier Trans Mountain consultation was unacceptably flawed because Canada's team acted essentially as note-takers rather than engaging in two-way dialogue (Tsleil-Waututh paras 557, 558 and 562).
definitions.PROP-13: The UNDRIP Act affirms the Declaration as a universal international human rights instrument with application in Canadian law and provides a framework for implementation (s. 4); the Government must take all measures necessary to ensure the laws of Canada are consistent with the Declaration (s. 5).
definitions.PROP-15: The Impact Assessment Act requires consideration of impacts on Indigenous groups and their rights and of Indigenous knowledge (s. 22(1)(c) and (g)); the Act's purposes include respecting the rights recognized and affirmed by s. 35 (s. 6(2)).
definitions.CONCLUSION-01: The regulator's approval decision is Crown conduct that triggers the duty, and the Crown may rely on an adequate regulatory process.
definitions.CONCLUSION-02: The Nation cannot insist on consent or a veto; adequate consultation and accommodation are the measure.
definitions.CLAIM-01: The duty to consult applies to Parliament's process of enacting legislation.
definitions.CLAIM-02: The UNDRIP Act makes the Declaration directly enforceable law that overrides inconsistent statutes.
definitions.CLAIM-03: The First Nation holds a veto over the pipeline approval.
definitions.CLAIM-04: The Crown must always conduct its own consultation separate from the regulator's process.
